The patient has a history of long-standing diplopia and an anomalous band in the right orbit, which was surgically excised without improvement in motility. This suggests a possible orbital pulley disorder.

The patient's history of long-standing diplopia, persistent vertical misalignment, and the presence of an anomalous band in the right orbit on MRI suggest Orbital Pulley Disorder. The fact that the diplopia remained stable in primary gaze and the patient had an elevation deficit of the right eye also supports this diagnosis.
